description: Rove's largest property by room count (579 keys); located within Dubai Parks and Resorts (theme park destination) and was Rove's sixth Dubai property at opening (June 2019).

venues.name: Daily at the Parks
venues.description: All-day dining restaurant with grab-and-go options for theme-park guests.

name: Ibis Styles Dubai Jumeira
address: Al Mina Road, 2nd December Street, Jumeira 1, Dubai, UAE
transit: Jafliya Metro Station (~5 km / ~15 min drive)
description: Design economy hotel; indoor pool; eco-certified; soft-opened 2018

venues.name: Khana Khazana
venues.description: Specialty Indian restaurant

venues.name: Street Café
venues.description: All-day dining restaurant with daily buffet breakfast and à la carte menu

name: Rove La Mer Beach
address: La Mer South, Jumeira 1, PO Box 119444, Dubai, UAE
description: Beachfront property inside the La Mer leisure destination (also referred to as J1 Beach), opened December 2020; access to 50+ restaurants across the wider La Mer complex.

venues.name: Drink Truck
venues.description: Casual outdoor drinks truck serving beverages on the hotel terrace overlooking the beach.

venues.name: Beach Bar
venues.description: Fully licensed poolside/sundeck bar with Arabian Gulf sunset views; in-room delivery available.

venues.name: The Daily
venues.description: All-day restaurant with breakfast buffet and freshly cooked dishes.

name: Ibis Dubai World Trade Centre
neighborhood: Sheikh Zayed Road, next to Dubai World Trade Centre
address: P.O. Box 9544, Sheikh Zayed Road, 9544, Dubai, United Arab Emirates
transit: World Trade Centre Metro Station (directly adjacent)
description: Economy-tier hotel directly beside World Trade Centre Metro Station; property states it has 3 restaurants and bars in total, of which 1 (Twine Restaurant) could be verified by name.

venues.name: Twine Restaurant
venues.description: All-day restaurant blending Mediterranean flavors and traditions; also serves the hotel's buffet breakfast.

name: Rove Downtown
address: 312 Al Mustaqbal Street, Za'abeel 2, Dubai, UAE
description: Rove's flagship debut property (May 2016); marketed as 'steps from Burj Khalifa/Downtown Dubai' though its Za'abeel 2 address is roughly 3km from Burj Khalifa - a common source of guest confusion with the actual Downtown Dubai district.

venues.name: The Daily
venues.description: Rove's signature all-day restaurant; breakfast buffet plus a la carte, licensed for beer/wine/spirits/cocktails.

name: Faena New York
description: Faena's first New York property (following the Miami Beach flagship), opened September 2025 in West Chelsea on the site of the long-stalled "XI"/One High Line development. Its Francis Mallmann restaurant here is branded "La Boca at Faena," distinct from Miami's "Los Fuegos." Room count not published on official site as of research date.

venues.name: El Secreto
venues.description: Hidden speakeasy-style bar with handcrafted cocktails.

venues.name: The Living Room
venues.description: Social cocktail lounge with nightly live music.

venues.name: La Boca at Faena by Francis Mallmann
venues.description: Francis Mallmann's wood-fire Argentine restaurant with nightly live music.

venues.name: La Cava
venues.description: Intimate wine-focused dining room.

name: Casa Cipriani New York
description: Occupies the landmarked Battery Maritime Building overlooking New York Harbor; opened August 2021 (fully finished December 2021) after a lease taken over by Cipriani S.A. in 2017. Combines a 47-suite boutique hotel with a private membership club and extensive Cipriani-branded dining and wellness facilities, several of which (5th floor venues) are members-oriented.

venues.name: Promenade Bar
venues.description: Bar with a gilt-edged mahogany counter and ocean-liner mural, serving as entrance to The Living Room.

venues.name: The Pickering Room
venues.description: All-day cafe for coffee and work that transitions into a dinner venue for larger groups.

venues.name: Wellness Cafe
venues.description: Members-only cafe within the hotel's 15,000-square-foot wellness facility.

venues.name: Jazz Cafe
venues.description: Supper club with nightly live jazz in a gold-leaf, 1930s-40s-styled room.

venues.name: Promenade Lounge
venues.description: Lounge with waterfront views, velvet banquettes and Art Deco-inspired fabrics.

venues.name: The Living Room
venues.description: Art Deco lounge with a fireplace offering pizzas, appetizers and full bar service through the day.

venues.name: West Terrace
venues.description: Rooftop-style terrace with Statue of Liberty and skyline views for coffee through evening cocktails.

venues.name: East Terrace
venues.description: Outdoor extension of The Restaurant with panoramic Brooklyn Bridge and East River views.

venues.name: The Restaurant
venues.description: Formal dining room styled after a 1930s French ocean liner, serving Cipriani classics such as carpaccio and baked tagliolini.

name: The Beekman, a Thompson Hotel
transit: Fulton Street (2, 3, 4, 5, A, C, J, Z)
description: Occupies the landmarked 1883 Temple Court building with its restored nine-story atrium and skylight. DISCREPANCY: dining lineup has changed since 2016 opening — original venues Augustine (Keith McNally) and the original Fowler & Wells concept have been superseded; the hotel's official site now lists Temple Court (Tom Colicchio) and Le Gratin (Daniel Boulud) as the current restaurants.

venues.name: The Bar Room
venues.description: Cocktail bar set beneath the ten-story atrium.

venues.name: Laissez Faire
venues.description: Industrial-luxe cocktail lounge in the historic Temple Court annex.

venues.name: Le Gratin
venues.description: Daniel Boulud's casual Lyonnais bouchon-style bistro.

venues.name: Temple Court
venues.description: Tom Colicchio's fine-dining restaurant beneath the hotel's historic atrium.

name: The Inn at Irving Place
description: Ultra-boutique inn spanning two restored 1834 townhouses, with no reception desk or elevator — rooms are reached via the original staircases. Dining includes Lady Mendl's Tea Salon (Victorian-style afternoon tea) and Cibar, an intimate lounge/garden bar.

venues.name: Cibar
venues.description: Intimate lounge/garden bar within the historic townhouses.

venues.name: Lady Mendl's Tea Salon
venues.description: Victorian-style afternoon tea salon in the historic townhouse.

name: Nine Orchard
brand: Independent (Leading Hotels of the World member)
description: Restored 1912 Jarmulowsky Bank building; the former bank's teller hall is now the Swan Room cocktail lounge, with marble walls and vaulted ceilings.

venues.name: Swan Room
venues.description: Opulent cocktail lounge and small-plates room set in the historic bank's marble-walled vault space.

venues.name: Corner Bar
venues.description: All-day neighborhood bistro and 40-seat bar serving breakfast through dinner.

name: Conrad New York Downtown
address: 102 North End Avenue, New York, NY 10282
description: All-suite luxury property in Battery Park City with an art-centric design concept and Hudson River views. Loopy Doopy Rooftop Bar is a well-known NYC rooftop destination.

venues.name: Loopy Doopy Rooftop Bar
venues.description: Rooftop bar serving innovative cocktails paired with skyline and harbor views; extended summer hours.

venues.name: ATRIO Wine Bar & Restaurant
venues.description: Mediterranean-inspired cuisine in a sleek, inviting atmosphere with locally sourced spirits at the bar.

name: Aman New York
description: Ultra-exclusive all-suite urban resort inside the landmarked Crown Building at Fifth Avenue and 57th Street, opened August 2022; includes a members' club, extensive spa, and a hidden speakeasy-style jazz club (The Tangiers).

venues.name: Corner Bar
venues.description: Refined bar overlooking the iconic Midtown Manhattan crossroads.

venues.name: Lounge Bar
venues.description: Central lounge offering cicchetti, sharing plates, craft cocktails and fine wines.

venues.name: The Jazz Club (The Tangiers)
venues.description: Speakeasy-style jazz club with curated live music, cocktails and small plates.

venues.name: Garden Terrace
venues.description: Year-round terrace with a retractable glass roof and firepits for light meals and cocktails.

venues.name: Akari
venues.description: Japanese washoku restaurant with a dedicated hinoki-wood omakase counter.

venues.name: Arva
venues.description: Rustic Italian restaurant inspired by the cucina del raccolto (harvest cooking) tradition.

name: Baccarat Hotel New York
description: Opened 2015 next to MoMA, the crystal maison's flagship hospitality venture with interiors by Gilles & Boissier; Grand Salon restaurant led by culinary director Gabriel Kreuther.

venues.name: The Bar
venues.description: Crystal-adorned cocktail bar featuring an art collection including works by Robert Longo.

venues.name: Grand Salon
venues.description: Fine-dining restaurant overseen by culinary director Gabriel Kreuther, centered on a signature Baccarat chandelier; also hosts afternoon tea.

venues.name: Le Jardin
venues.description: Additional dining venue listed on the hotel's official dining menu; detailed cuisine and concept not confirmed from sources checked.

name: Four Seasons Hotel New York
description: I.M. Pei-designed 52-story tower that opened in 1993; closed in 2020 for extensive renovation and reopened November 2024 under owner Ty Warner Hotels and Resorts. Dining is currently limited to two venues post-renovation.

venues.name: TY Bar
venues.description: Art Deco-inspired cocktail bar showcasing drinks from different eras of New York history.

venues.name: The Garden
venues.description: Art Deco-inspired restaurant with acacia trees overlooking 57th Street, serving seasonal fare.

name: JW Marriott Essex House New York
address: 160 Central Park South, New York, NY 10019
description: DISCREPANCY/STATUS: Historic 1931 Art Deco tower (Historic Hotels of America member) managed as Jumeirah Essex House from 2006 until it converted to the JW Marriott flag around 2016-2017. Its 3-Michelin-starred Alain Ducasse at Essex House closed in 2007 and was replaced by the current Southgate Bar & Restaurant in 2008. Famous for its red neon rooftop sign facing Central Park.

venues.name: Southgate Bar & Restaurant
venues.description: Casual American restaurant and bar with Central Park views, opened in 2008 in the space that once housed the 3-Michelin-starred Alain Ducasse at Essex House.

name: Mandarin Oriental, New York
description: STATUS: Occupies the upper floors (35th and above) of the Deutsche Bank Center (formerly Time Warner Center) overlooking Central Park; opened December 2003. Its long-running signature restaurant Asiate has closed and been replaced by MO Lounge, with a new venue, The Bar, launching September 2025 — the dining lineup here has changed materially from its original opening era.

venues.name: The Bar
venues.description: New cocktail bar at the hotel that debuted in September 2025.

venues.name: MO Lounge
venues.description: All-day restaurant and cocktail venue with Central Park views, successor to the former Asiate restaurant.

name: Park Hyatt New York
description: Hyatt's New York flagship, occupying the lower floors of the One57 tower; opened 2014 with interiors by Yabu Pushelberg and Central Park views.

venues.name: The Living Room
venues.description: Upscale all-day restaurant and bar styled after the ambience of a Central Park residence.

name: The Langham, New York, Fifth Avenue
transit: 34 St-Herald Sq (B, D, F, M, N, Q, R, W)
description: Opened in late 2010 on Fifth Avenue near the Empire State Building; home to the Michelin-starred Ai Fiori restaurant. Exact current total room count could not be confirmed from sources checked.

venues.name: Bar Fiori
venues.description: Bar and lounge adjoining Ai Fiori offering cocktails, wine and small plates.

venues.name: Ai Fiori
venues.description: Michelin-starred coastal European restaurant led by Chef de Cuisine Scott Schneider.

name: The Peninsula New York
brand: The Peninsula Hotels (Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels, Ltd.)
description: Beaux-Arts building originally opened in 1905 as the Gotham Hotel, relaunched as The Peninsula New York in 1989; underwent a major renovation completed 2023-2024. Known for its rooftop Pen Top bar.

venues.name: Pen Top
venues.description: Rooftop bar with cocktails and skyline views over Fifth Avenue.

venues.name: The Bar at Clement
venues.description: Upscale cocktail lounge overlooking Fifth Avenue, known for a Martini & Caviar pairing.

venues.name: Gotham Lounge
venues.description: Lounge known for its legendary afternoon tea service.

venues.name: Clement
venues.description: All-day New American restaurant and the hotel's main dining room.

name: The Plaza
brand: Fairmont Hotels & Resorts (owned by Katara Hospitality)
description: STATUS: National Historic Landmark opened in 1907 at Grand Army Plaza; a 2008 renovation converted much of the building to a hybrid hotel/condominium (282 hotel rooms plus 181 condos). Several historic dining venues from the hotel's past (the Oak Room, Persian Room, and the more recent Todd English Food Hall) are no longer listed as operating; current official dining is limited to the Palm Court and Champagne Bar.

venues.name: The Champagne Bar
venues.description: Bar for fine champagnes, wines and caviar overlooking Fifth Avenue and the Pulitzer Fountain.

venues.name: The Palm Court
venues.description: The Plaza's iconic tea room and restaurant, serving afternoon tea and evening dining with a cocktail program.

name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park
address: 50 Central Park South, New York, NY 10019
description: Overlooks Central Park South; converted from the historic 1930 Hotel St. Moritz and reopened as The Ritz-Carlton in 2002. Operates as a hybrid hotel/condominium (Millennium Partners owns the building; Ritz-Carlton manages the hotel).

venues.name: Contour
venues.description: All-day social dining restaurant and bar pairing handcrafted cocktails with refined American dishes.

name: The St. Regis New York
description: Beaux-Arts flagship of the St. Regis brand, opened 1904 at Fifth Avenue and 55th Street; owned by Qatar Investment Authority since 2019 and managed by Marriott. Home to the historic King Cole Bar beneath Maxfield Parrish's 1906 mural.

venues.name: King Cole Bar
venues.description: Historic bar beneath Maxfield Parrish's mural, birthplace of the Red Snapper (Bloody Mary) cocktail.

venues.name: The Drawing Room
venues.location: Ground floor, adjacent to King Cole Bar
venues.description: Reimagined velvet-appointed lounge serving shareable bites and large plates.

venues.name: La Maisonette
venues.description: Bright, pavilion-style restaurant serving breakfast, lunch and afternoon tea.

name: The Whitby Hotel
description: Boutique Firmdale Hotels property (Tim and Kit Kemp) near MoMA, opened 2017, with an in-house screening room; dining is centered on a single all-day bar and restaurant.

venues.name: The Whitby Bar & Restaurant
venues.description: All-day bar and restaurant known for its pewter-topped bar and 'Jazz & Oysters' evenings.

name: Waldorf Astoria New York
description: STATUS: Art Deco landmark originally opened October 1931; closed in 2017 for an eight-year renovation and reopened July 2025 with only 375 hotel rooms (down from roughly 1,400), the rest of the tower converted to condominium residences. Some historic dining names from before the closure, including the famed Bull and Bear Steakhouse and La Chine, do not appear on the hotel's current official dining page and their reopening status could not be confirmed from sources checked.

venues.name: Lex Yard
venues.description: Brasserie-style restaurant led by James Beard Award-winning Chef Michael Anthony, in an Art Deco setting.

venues.name: Peacock Alley
venues.description: Iconic restaurant and bar named for the hotel's storied Peacock Alley corridor, with all-day dining and a full bar.

venues.name: Yoshoku
venues.description: Fine-dining Japanese restaurant offering a kaiseki-inspired menu reimagined through a New York lens.

name: Conrad New York Midtown
description: Newer Conrad property (opened 2023) offering a residential-style aesthetic in Midtown Manhattan.

venues.name: Dabble
venues.description: Eclectic bites and a buzzing nightly bar scene just off the hotel lobby.

name: InterContinental New York Barclay
description: Historic hotel opened in 1926 as part of the Grand Central Terminal-area development, once featuring its own private rail platform for guests. Currently undergoing guestroom modernization.

venues.name: The Parlour
venues.description: "1920's Manhattan Glamour" restaurant and bar with elevated seasonal fare from locally sourced, organic ingredients; rooftop gardens and beehives supply the kitchen; hosts Oyster Hour and live jazz programming.

name: Park Lane New York
address: 36 Central Park South, New York, NY 10019
description: Luxury 1971 tower directly on Central Park South, a Preferred Hotels & Resorts member with notable dining including Darling Rooftop (47th floor, the only rooftop lounge on Central Park South), Rose Lane, and Calvert's. STATUS: Qatar Investment Authority bought the hotel in August 2023 ($623M) and announced 2025 plans to redevelop the property into a luxury hotel-and-condominium project; the hotel is currently still operating and bookable, but a future closure for redevelopment should be expected and monitored.

venues.name: Rose Lane
venues.description: Parisian art-nouveau-inspired all-day cafe with cozy corners for morning coffee, al fresco lunch, or a nightcap.

venues.name: Darling Rooftop
venues.description: The only rooftop lounge on Central Park South; whimsical space with curated cocktails and sweeping Manhattan skyline views.

venues.name: Calvert's
venues.description: Newer restaurant concept reimagining the flavors and dining experience of the Central Park South area.

venues.name: In-Room Dining
venues.description: In-room dining service available to guests.

name: The Chatwal
description: DISCREPANCY: The source list identifies this as "The Chatwal, a Luxury Collection Hotel" (Marriott), but the property left Marriott's Luxury Collection following a December 2023 ownership change and is now branded The Chatwal, by Hyatt under Hyatt's Unbound Collection. STATUS: The hotel's historic signature restaurant, The Lambs Club (opened 2010, reopened 2022 under chef Michael White), is no longer listed as an active venue on the hotel's current official (Hyatt) site; current official dining is provided via a partnership with The Long Room, an Irish gastropub adjacent to the hotel — Lambs Club's current operating status could not be confirmed and may have closed.

venues.name: The Long Room
venues.description: Hotel's current official dining partner; an Irish gastropub inspired by the library at Trinity College Dublin, offering contemporary American and Irish fare, craft cocktails, and an extensive whiskey selection.

name: The Knickerbocker Hotel
brand: Independent (The Leading Hotels of the World; managed by Highgate)
address: 6 Times Square (142 West 42nd Street), New York, NY 10036
description: Landmark 1906 building atop Times Square, restored and reopened as a luxury hotel in 2015 under The Leading Hotels of the World; not a Marriott/Hilton/IHG brand despite being grouped with them in the source list. Rooftop bar St. Cloud offers panoramic Times Square views.

venues.name: St. Cloud Rooftop Bar
venues.description: Rooftop bar with sweeping Times Square views, inventive cocktails, and refined small plates.

venues.name: The Martini Lounge
venues.description: Cocktail lounge in the hotel lobby.

venues.name: Akoya
venues.description: Sushi bar within the hotel.

venues.name: Charlie Palmer Steak
venues.description: Fine-dining steakhouse from chef Charlie Palmer serving "Honest American Cuisine."

name: The Times Square EDITION
description: STATUS: Opened February 2019, closed permanently in August 2020 amid ownership/lender financial distress worsened by the pandemic; officially confirmed reopened for both NYC EDITION properties (Times Square and Madison Square Park) in 2021 and is currently operating. Michelin-starred chef John Fraser oversees all food and beverage outlets, including The Terrace restaurant and Paradise Club nightlife venue.

venues.name: Lobby Bar
venues.description: Upscale pre-theater lounge with white furniture and custom leather armchairs overlooking Times Square.

venues.name: Paradise Club
venues.description: High-energy entertainment venue offering dinner shows, dancing, and signature parties.

venues.name: The Terrace and Outdoor Gardens
venues.description: American brasserie classics with a vegetable-forward approach and locally sourced ingredients; outdoor garden seating in the Theater District. Helmed by chef John Fraser.

name: The Fifth Avenue Hotel
brand: Independent (Leading Hotels of the World member)
description: Note: located in NoMad, just north of the core downtown boutique cluster covered by this list. Combines a restored Gilded Age mansion with a new 24-story tower; named a "One to Watch" in The World's 50 Best Hotels 2026. Room count sources vary slightly (153 per Forbes Travel Guide vs. 104 per LHW) — 153 used here as the more commonly cited figure.

venues.name: The Portrait Bar
venues.description: Wood-paneled cocktail bar with a stone fireplace and elevated bar fare.

venues.name: Café Carmellini
venues.description: Chef Andrew Carmellini's celebrated fine-dining restaurant.

name: The Ned NoMad
brand: The Ned (Sydell Group / Soho House Ned's Club joint venture)
description: ANSWER to naming question 3: The Ned NoMad occupies the same historic Johnston Building as the original NoMad Hotel, which closed permanently in March 2021; the space was reopened in July 2022 as The Ned NoMad, the New York outpost of the London-founded 'Ned' concept (a hotel-and-private-members-club hybrid curated by Richie Akiva), an entirely different brand and operator from Sydell's original 'NoMad' hotel brand. Most of the club-level venues are members-only; Cecconi's restaurant is open to the public.

venues.name: Little Ned
venues.description: Two-story, 1920s-inspired pub-style bar for club members and hotel guests, with mezzanine seating overlooking the Empire State Building; classic bar fare and cocktails.

venues.name: The Rooftop
venues.description: Members-only rooftop bar and lounge space with Manhattan skyline views.

venues.name: Ned's Club
venues.location: Off the lobby (multi-room, includes The Magic Room cabaret on the 2nd floor and a members' Library/Dining Room)
venues.description: Private members' club at the heart of the property, with an atrium/garden space that transitions into an evening lounge with live performances; includes the Art Deco-inspired Magic Room cabaret and a dedicated members' dining room.

venues.name: Cecconi's
venues.description: Manhattan's first Cecconi's location; a mid-century-inspired Northern Italian trattoria open to the public for breakfast, lunch and dinner (beef tartare, wood-fired pizzas, pastas).

name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, NoMad
description: Ritz-Carlton's NoMad 'urban resort' opened in 2022, featuring 219 rooms and 31 suites (plus 14 separately sold penthouse residences) and multiple José Andrés restaurant concepts, including the rooftop Nubeluz bar.

venues.name: Bazaar Bar
venues.description: Library-style bar offering hand-crafted cocktails and appetizers.

venues.name: Nubeluz
venues.description: Rooftop cocktail bar dubbed 'a lightbox in the sky' with 270-degree skyline views.

venues.name: The Lobby Lounge
venues.description: All-day cafe and lounge serving pastries and coffee by day, cocktails by night.

venues.name: Bazaar Meat
venues.description: Theatrical José Andrés steakhouse built around wood-fired cooking and bold flavors.

venues.name: Zaytinya
venues.description: José Andrés' all-day restaurant serving mezze inspired by Turkish, Greek and Lebanese cuisines.

name: Crosby Street Hotel
description: British-owned boutique hotel with individually designed rooms by co-owner Kit Kemp; The Crosby Bar functions as the hotel's restaurant/bar with an ivy-laden terrace and sculpture garden.

venues.name: The Crosby Bar
venues.description: All-day bar and restaurant with a brasserie menu opening onto an ivy-laden terrace.

name: The Mercer
description: Opened 1997 as "SoHo's first hotel," originally developed by André Balazs. DISCREPANCY: the long-running ground-floor restaurant Mercer Kitchen (Jean-Georges Vongerichten) has been replaced by Sartiano's at The Mercer (Scott Sartiano and Chef Alfred Portale), a modern Italian concept, per the current official site.

venues.name: Sartiano's at The Mercer
venues.description: Modern Italian restaurant from Scott Sartiano and Chef Alfred Portale, successor to the longtime Mercer Kitchen.

name: Hotel Barrière Fouquet's New York
description: French luxury group Barrière's first U.S. hotel, an homage to its iconic Fouquet's Paris brasserie (est. 1899); includes a rooftop bar (Le Vaux) and spa/DOGPOUND fitness center.

venues.name: Le Vaux Rooftop
venues.description: Seasonal rooftop bar blending Parisian elegance with New York industrial style.

venues.name: Titsou Bar
venues.description: 1920s-30s Paris-inspired speakeasy-style cocktail bar.

venues.name: Brasserie Fouquet's
venues.description: Classic French brasserie paying homage to the original 1899 Fouquet's Paris.

venues.name: Élysée's
venues.description: All-day Mediterranean dining inspired by the southern coasts of Italy and France.

name: The Greenwich Hotel
description: Tribeca boutique hotel co-owned by Robert De Niro, opened 2008 with eclectic interiors by designer Axel Vervoordt and architect Tatsuro Miki; home to Andrew Carmellini's Locanda Verde.

venues.name: Locanda Verde
venues.description: Andrew Carmellini's celebrated Italian restaurant off the Greenwich Hotel lobby.

name: Loews Regency New York
address: 540 Park Avenue at 61st Street, New York, NY 10065
description: Storied Upper East Side luxury hotel famous for hosting the original "Power Breakfast" at The Regency Bar & Grill. DISCREPANCY: the source list associates this hotel with "Feinstein's/54 Below" cabaret, but the hotel's current official dining pages make no mention of Feinstein's — that cabaret venue (Feinstein's/54 Below) is a separate, unaffiliated Manhattan club on West 54th Street, and the hotel's earlier in-house cabaret room ("Feinstein's at the Regency") closed years ago. Current confirmed dining is The Regency Bar & Grill and the standalone Sant Ambroeus Coffee Bar.

venues.name: Sant Ambroeus Coffee Bar
venues.location: Ground floor, separate entrance on East 61st Street
venues.description: Standalone Milanese-style café serving espresso, pastries, and sandwiches; take-out focused, run by the Sant Ambroeus brand.

venues.name: The Regency Bar & Grill
venues.description: Home of the original "Power Breakfast"; serves breakfast, brunch, lunch, and dinner in a quintessential Upper East Side setting, with private event capacity for 10-275 guests.

name: The Carlyle, A Rosewood Hotel
description: Legendary Upper East Side hotel opened in 1930, long favored by presidents and celebrities; Rosewood-owned and operated since 2001. World-famous for Bemelmans Bar's Ludwig Bemelmans murals and Cafe Carlyle's cabaret performances.

venues.name: Bemelmans Bar
venues.description: Iconic cocktail bar famed for Ludwig Bemelmans' murals and nightly piano and jazz.

venues.name: The Gallery
venues.description: Jewel-box lounge designed by Renzo Mongiardino offering afternoon tea and light refreshments.

venues.name: Cafe Carlyle
venues.description: Intimate, last-of-its-kind supper club presenting nightly cabaret and live entertainment.

venues.name: Dowling's at The Carlyle
venues.description: Contemporary American restaurant with tableside preparations, surrounded by works from over 200 local artists.

name: The Lowell
brand: Independent (Leading Hotels of the World member; owned by Fouad Chartouni)
description: Intimate townhouse-style hotel between Madison and Park Avenues, originally opened in 1927 and given a $25 million renovation (interiors by Michael S. Smith) that reopened in 2017.

venues.name: Jacques Bar
venues.description: Hotel bar serving classic and seasonal cocktails.

venues.name: The Club Room
venues.description: Clubby lounge and bar space at the hotel.

venues.name: Majorelle
venues.description: Moroccan/Mediterranean-inspired restaurant led by Executive Chef David Thual, evoking Marrakesh gardens.

venues.name: Pembroke Room
venues.description: Elegant dining room known for its afternoon tea service.

name: The Mark
description: Storied Madison Avenue townhouse-style hotel favored by fashion and entertainment figures; originally opened in 1927 as the Hyde Park Hotel and reimagined in 2009 by designer Jacques Grange. Home to Jean-Georges Vongerichten's restaurant and the celebrated Mark Bar. Independently owned by Alexico Group, not part of a major hotel chain.

venues.name: The Mark Bar
venues.description: Stylish first-come, first-served cocktail bar popular for after-work gatherings.

venues.name: The Mark Hot Dog Cart
venues.description: Seasonal Jean-Georges-curated hot dog cart operated outside the hotel, weather permitting.

venues.name: Caviar Kaspia at The Mark
venues.description: New York outpost of the legendary Paris caviar restaurant, known for its twice-baked potato with caviar.

venues.name: The Mark Restaurant by Jean-Georges
venues.location: Ground floor, Madison Avenue at 77th St
venues.description: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's all-day restaurant with indoor and outdoor seating designed by Jacques Grange.

name: The Pierre, A Taj Hotel
description: Historic 41-story tower at Fifth Avenue and 61st Street overlooking Central Park, opened in 1930; operated by Taj Hotels since 2005. Known for the murals of The Rotunda and its Perrine restaurant.

venues.name: Two E Bar and Lounge
venues.description: Bar and lounge serving cocktails and casual bites.

venues.name: The Rotunda
venues.description: Domed, muraled room historically known for the hotel's afternoon tea service.

venues.name: Perrine
venues.description: Fine-dining restaurant serving French-American cuisine.

name: The Surrey, A Corinthia Hotel
description: DISCREPANCY: The list name 'The Surrey, a Corinthia Hotel' is confirmed as the hotel's current official branding (rebranded from the long-independent 'The Surrey'). Its former long-standing restaurant Cafe Boulud (Daniel Boulud) and Bar Pleiades no longer appear on the property's current pages, replaced by Casa Tua; the exact rebrand/reopening year could not be confirmed from official sources checked (WebFetch access issues prevented full verification), so year_opened is left n/a pending confirmation.

venues.name: Casa Tua
venues.description: Restaurant, lounge and members' club serving Italian and Mediterranean cuisine.

name: citizenM New York Bowery

name: Grand Prince Hotel Shin Takanawa (formerly marketed as Grand Prince Hotel New Takanawa)
description: DISCREPANCY: the brief for this research flagged 'Grand Prince Hotel New Takanawa' as having closed permanently in March 2021. Direct verification of the official Prince Hotels site (princehotels.com/shintakanawa/) as of this research shows the hotel currently OPEN and operating — 908 guest rooms, an active booking engine, and live operational notices (e.g. WiFi maintenance windows). 'Shin Takanawa' (新高輪) is simply the modern official English rendering of '(New) Takanawa'; no evidence of a 2021 permanent closure of this tower was found. The 2021 closure claim likely conflates this property with the separate Grand Prince Hotel Akasaka (Chiyoda-ku), which did close permanently on March 31, 2011. Designed by architect Togo Murano and opened in 1982 on the former Takanawa Golf Center site; largest of the three connected Takanawa towers, with ~20,000 sq m shared Japanese garden.
